key_insight: Sparse autoencoders can be turned into local, low-rank geometric constraints that reduce catastrophic forgetting while preserving plasticity in continual learning.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical stability-plasticity mechanism for deployed learning systems that must adapt to new data without losing prior task performance.
method: Train a Sparse Autoencoder at each task boundary.
Use replay samples to localize where representation drift should be constrained.
Penalize drift along the encoder Jacobian’s leading right singular directions, then discard the SAE for later training.
evidence_signal: On pretrained ViT-B/16 benchmarks, the method achieved the best mean Class-IL accuracy and lowest mean forgetting, with gains of 12.15, 4.79, and 3.22 points over the strongest conventional baseline on CIFAR-100, CUB-200, and ImageNet-R.
watch_item: Benefits are more mixed when training from scratch, so the geometry constraints may be more sensitive to backbone pretraining and rank choices.
paper_title: Sparse Autoencoders Can Induce Local Geometry for Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting
